title: Feeding Schedule Drift
dataSources: Pet tracker location/activity (`tractive:position`, `whistle:activity`), smart feeder events (`petfeeder:event`), litter-box usage (`litterrobot:cycle`), bird-feeder detections (`birdfeeder:detection`), doorbell/package events (`doorbell:event`).
app: Pet GPS/activity trackers (Tractive/Fi/Whistle), smart feeders and litter boxes, bird feeders/cams, and home-life sensors via vendor APIs and MQTT to HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=petfeeder:event event_type=dispense
| eval feed_hour=strftime(_time,"%H")
| bin _time span=1d
| stats avg(feed_hour) as avg_hour, stdev(feed_hour) as hour_sd by feeder _time
| where hour_sd>1.5
| sort - hour_sd
description: Measures how stable the actual dispense times are day to day, helping you verify that feeding automation follows the routine you thought you set.
value: Pets thrive on consistency, and smart feeders can drift because of config changes, manual overrides, or failed schedules; this query makes that visible.
implementation: Forward dispense events from the feeder; review daily schedule variance and tighten timers if needed.
visualization: Daily chart of average feeding hour and timing variability.
grandmaExplanation: It surfaces when the automatic feeder starts giving meals at noticeably inconsistent times.
